create.name: Zen Buddhism Ireland
create.bio:
Zen Buddhism Ireland is a Soto Zen sangha based in Dublin, whose practice home, the Dublin Zen Centre, is in Temple Bar, with members elsewhere in Ireland joining online. It stands in the lineage of Gudo Nishijima. Its founding teacher and abbot is Rev. Myozan Kodo Kilroy (Myozan Ian Kilroy), a former journalist and published poet who received transmission from Taigu Turlur and belongs to the Soto Zen Buddhist Association. Two of his students, Hodo Gomoku and Kozan Kokai, have since become transmitted teachers, and a small group of priests and priests in training serve the sangha with them.

The practice centres on shikantaza, just sitting, kept within the traditional forms of Zen and with particular care given to sewing the okesa, the robe of the Buddha. In Temple Bar there are sittings on Monday and Wednesday evenings and on Saturday mornings, each with walking meditation, a short chanting service and a talk or discussion, plus a day-long zazenkai on the last Sunday of the month. An online zendo opens every morning and on Monday evenings, and the website and Myozan's YouTube channel offer instruction in posture, breathing, walking meditation and oryoki meals.

courses.title: Practice at the Dublin Zen Centre
courses.description: Sittings in Temple Bar on Monday and Wednesday evenings and Saturday mornings: two periods of silent zazen with walking meditation between, a short chanting service and a talk or discussion. First-timers are asked to arrive early for guidance, and a monthly day-long zazenkai is held on the last Sunday.

free_resources.title: Online Zendo
free_resources.description: Half-hour morning sittings on Zoom every day, with a short chanting service, and a longer Monday evening session with a sharing circle or talk; the page links the etiquette guide and chant book.

free_resources.title: How to Sit
free_resources.description: Myozan's video instruction on the body, breath and mind in zazen, alongside Dogen's Fukanzazengi in the Nishijima and Cross translation.

free_resources.title: RTE Documentary
free_resources.description: A short television documentary, shown with the broadcaster's permission, following the sangha as it marks the opening of its Temple Bar centre with a Buddha Day ceremony.

flags: Email myozankodo@gmail.com is the guiding teacher's own address, published on the Online Zendo page for questions; the home page also has a contact form (Squarespace, rendered by script).
YouTube: the channel is the guiding teacher's (Myozan Kodo), described as based in Dublin with zenbuddhism.ie; the online-practice guide video is on priest Kozan Kokai's channel.
Base: the Dublin Zen Centre is now at Anglesea St, Temple Bar (the SZBA list shows an older Eustace St address).
Photos: the sangha in robes outdoors, a carved Jizo statue, and a black-and-white shot of the sangha at a retreat table; all from zenbuddhism.ie.
Founded year left null: not stated on the site.
Myozan Kodo Kilroy has written books (Do Not Try to Become a Buddha, Three Rock Sonnets, Songs from the Denkoroku) and could be a future individual listing.
Teachers file empty: Myozan Kodo Kilroy, Hodo Gomoku and Kozan Kokai are not on Spiritpedia.
